title: Investigate credential-rollover-induced cross-tenant billing spike affecting ephemeral subaccounts
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported unexplained bill increases coincident with a scheduled credential rollover for delegated ephemeral subaccounts. Symptoms include duplicated token-level metering events and incorrect tenant attribution (requests counted against both parent org and ephemeral subaccount). This ticket tracks root-cause analysis, mitigation, and permanent fixes for attribution correctness during credential rotation flows.
reproduction_steps:
1) Create a parent org with an ephemeral subaccount that uses delegated proxy tokens (ephemeral_token_v2).
2) Start steady traffic through the proxy using the old token.
3) Trigger the credential rollover (automated rotation job) which issues a new ephemeral token and updates the tenant-binding in tenant-mapper service.
4) Observe metering events emitted during the 30s window around rotation.
Expected: All events map to either old token (until rotation completes) or to new token after mapping update.
Observed: ~0.5% of requests are duplicated into two metering events and attributed to both tenants OR attributed solely to the wrong tenant, causing over-billing for some customers.
investigation_notes:
- Logs: ingress-proxy showed two downstream calls for a small subset of requests where the proxy retried an upstream call that completed but emitted a redundant metering record.
- Metering pipeline: the collector receives the same request_id twice with different tenant_id headers in a 100ms window. The request-level signature differs by the ephemeral token id.
- Tenant-mapper: there is a race where token->tenant binding is updated atomically in Redis, but an upstream cache in rate-limiter reads stale mapping while metering collector reads the new mapping, producing divergent attribution.
- Rate limiter: owner attribution uses a long-lived in-memory cache keyed by token prefix; cache invalidation on rotation was best-effort and misses in a subset of hosts.
- RPC chronology: rotation job updates KMS/HSM and then writes the binding; some replicas processed traffic during a cross-region propagation delay.
- Impact scope: ~0.6% of hostnames during the 2026-02-14 rotation window. Affected customers are a mix of self-serve and committed Dedicated tenants (3 high-volume customers flagged).
- Historical similarity: similar pattern to previous 'key-swap' incidents but with differences: duplication of metering events rather than simple mis-bind. See related tickets: ENG-31228, ENG-5721 for context on attribution races.
root_cause_hypothesis: A combination of (1) non-atomic metadata flip for token->tenant binding across services, (2) asynchronous cache invalidation in the rate-limiter/inference-proxy fleet, and (3) a metering collector dedup path that keyed on token id only (not request_id + canonical binding). During rollover a small window exists where different services resolve the same request to different tenant identities and both sides emit valid metering events leading to double-credits to billing pipeline.
proposed_solution:
Short-term mitigations (1) emergency reconciliation job to de-dupe recent metering batches for the affected time window and backfill correct tenant attribution; (2) blacklist the specific rotation window from invoice generation until reconciliation completes; (3) push fix to rotation job to perform a two-phase commit: write new binding to tenant-mapper with an explicit version field and only flip the active flag after propagation confirmations.

Permanent fixes (1) change metering collector to compute final tenant attribution by resolving request_id -> token -> binding at ingest time using the authoritative tenant-mapper (with TTL/consistent read) and drop duplicate events where request_id matches but tenant differs within N seconds window; (2) update rate-limiter cache to include token binding version and add short-circuit on rotation events to force authoritative lookup for token age < rotation_safety_window; (3) add strong instrumentation and event tracing during rotations (rotation_id traced through logs/metrics).
rollout_plan: 1) Reconciliation job (billing pipeline) - run in staging, validate against synthetic rotated traffic. 2) Deploy collector change behind feature flag to 5% canary (non-customer impacting telemetry first). 3) Deploy authoritative read and cache-versioning to rate-limiter and proxy behind feature flag and enable for 5% of hosts. 4) Perform coordinated credential-rollover on a canary org to validate stability. 5) Ramp to 25% -> 100% while monitoring attribution-sanity dashboards and billing deltas. 6) After successful ramp, run reconciliation for production window and release billing credits if required.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests: token binding versioning, dedup logic keyed by request_id + token + timestamp.
- Integration tests: synthetic traffic across rotation event with varying latencies; assert single metering event per request_id.
- Chaos test: induce rotation propagation delays between replica regions while exercising high TPS to ensure no duplication.
- Load test: validate collector performance with extra authoritative lookups at expected QPS.
- Regression: run historical rotation events regression harness (using captured traces) to verify no re-introduction.
monitoring_and_alerts:
- New metrics: attribution_conflicts_count (per-tenant, per-hour), duplicate_metering_rate, token_binding_version_mismatch_rate.
- Dashboards: per-rotation_id heatmap of conflicts, customer-level billing-delta.
- Alerts: P1 if duplicate_metering_rate > 0.1% for > 10 minutes or attribution_conflicts_count spikes for committed tenants.
- Postmortem: prepare a customer-facing writeup and internal RCA after reconciliation completes.
rollback_plan: If the collector change causes latency regressions or ingestion instability, revert feature flag and fallback to current dedup logic; abort rotation deployments until fix is stabilized. Reconciliation job can be re-run incrementally; ensure billing generation is gated until reconciled.
metrics_to_track:
- Duplicate metering events per million requests.
- Net billing delta by customer over affected window.
- Token binding propagation 95th percentile latency.
- Rate-limiter cache miss rate during rotation windows.
- Ingest latency added by authoritative mapping lookups.
estimated_work_breakdown:
- Investigation & reproducible test harness: 2 pts (2d)
- Collector dedup & authoritative lookup: 5 pts (1w)
- Rate-limiter cache versioning & invalidation: 3 pts (4d)
- Reconciliation job & billing backfill tooling: 4 pts (1w)
- Testing, canary rollout, monitoring: 3 pts (4d)

acceptance_criteria:
1) No duplicate metering events produced for synthetic rotation tests.
2) Production canary shows duplicate_metering_rate < 0.01% and attribution_conflicts_count ~= 0 for 48h.
3) Reconciliation job can identify and reassign misattributed events with an audit log; finance signs off on credits/backfill logic.
4) New rotation observability dashboards display rotation_id traces for stakeholders.
customer_communication: Draft a short incident notice to affected customers explaining: what happened, scope, actions taken (temporary suspension of invoicing for window X), expected timeline for reconciliation, and contact for billing support. Share a more detailed RCA after reconciliation completes.
